why: Point update and range query, where the query is not a plain sum: the weighted sum splits into sum p*a[p] - (l-1)*sum a[p], so two Fenwick trees (one over a[p], one over p*a[p]) answer it.
hints: The weight of position p in query [l, r] is p - l + 1. Can you split that into a part that depends only on p and a part that depends only on l?
sum (p - l + 1) * a[p] = sum p*a[p] - (l - 1) * sum a[p] over p in [l, r]. Both sums are range sums of arrays that change only at single points.
Keep two Fenwick trees, for a[p] and p*a[p]. An update adds (v - old) and p*(v - old); a query takes the two range sums and combines them. O(log n) each.
pitfalls: An update replaces the value: add the difference, not the new value.
